This valuation gap is further highlighted by the company’s P/E ratio of 18.56x, which remains notably more attractive than the sector benchmark of 24.92x [E6]. The most compelling evidence for future potential is the massive 218.1% increase in capital work in progress (CWIP) to Rs 22.65 Cr, signaling a substantial growth-oriented investment phase [E32]. While the company has demonstrated a strong 21% compounded profit growth over the last three years [E16], it is currently positioned near the bottom of its 52-week range [E5], suggesting the market has yet to price in the impact of these ongoing capital expenditures.
